It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

branch_014.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The actor 'External Maintenance Personnel' has a single end-to-end intention: to manage assigned reports from receipt through resolution. The current hierarchy fragments this into three distinct HLGs: 'Receive Assigned Tasks', 'Update Work Status', and 'Communicate with Technical Office'. 'Update Work Status' is a specific workflow phase (state transition) that is part of the broader management process. It is not an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome separate from the overall goal of ensuring resolution. Since 'Update Work Status' is a narrow phase and the hierarchy is fragmented without a valid umbrella goal, it should be removed in favor of consolidating the actor's goals under a broader intention (likely by rewriting 'Receive Assigned Tasks' or creating a new umbrella, but for this specific artifact, it is a redundant fragment).

The original goal 'Configure System Settings' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly mentions that the municipal administrator can configure automatic assignment rules. However, the actor description defines the Municipal Administrator as responsible for 'system configuration, user management, and accessing private statistics.' branch_017.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' is supported by the documentation, which states that the private section accessible to administrators allows viewing charts and tables in addition to public statistics. The actor description explicitly lists 'accessing private statistics' as a responsibility. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Analyze System Operational Data' is semantically equivalent to the original goal, as viewing detailed charts and tables for oversight constitutes analyzing operational data. There are no other sibling goals for the Municipal Administrator that cover this statistical oversight intention (the other goal is 'Configure System Settings'). Therefore, the goal is correctly scoped, supported, and independent. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The documentation explicitly states that the private section accessible to administrators allows viewing 'charts and tables' in addition to public statistics. It does not mention the ability to generate custom reports, export data to external formats, or view interactive dashboards with KPIs. The current LLGs (llg_002, llg_003, llg_004) introduce capabilities that are not supported by the provided project description. While 'RetrieveAllReportStatistics' (llg_001) is partially supported, the presence of unsupported LLGs requires regeneration to align strictly with the documented functionality of viewing charts and tables.

low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback: Remove unsupported capabilities for generating custom reports, exporting data, and viewing dashboards. Focus the LLGs on retrieving and viewing the documented private statistics, specifically charts and tables, which are explicitly mentioned as available in the administrator's private section.

branch_018.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Process Citizen Reports' is redundant and overly broad. The documentation explicitly defines the Organization Office Staff's role as performing a 'preliminary review' to mark reports as 'accepted or rejected'. This specific intention is already captured by the sibling goal 'Approve or Reject Reports'. The original goal 'Process Citizen Reports' implies a broader lifecycle management (including transitions to In Progress, etc.), which is actually the responsibility of the Technical Office Staff (as seen in their goals 'Assign Approved Reports', 'Update Report Status'). The Organization Office Staff does not manage the full workflow; they only handle the initial decision. Therefore, 'Process Citizen Reports' is either a duplicate of 'Approve or Reject Reports' or an incorrect attribution of the full workflow management to the wrong actor. Since 'Approve or Reject Reports' accurately captures the documented intention, 'Process Citizen Reports' should be removed to avoid redundancy and scope confusion.

Therefore, 'Process Citizen Reports' is either a duplicate of 'Approve or Reject Reports' or an incorrect attribution of the full workflow management to the wrong actor. Since 'Approve or Reject Reports' accurately captures the documented intention, 'Process Citizen Reports' should be removed to avoid redundancy and scope confusion.

branch_019.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is supported by the documentation. The project description explicitly states that citizens can receive updates regarding their own reports, view status changes, and disable email notifications in the user settings panel. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Control Information Flow Regarding Their Submitted Reports' is semantically equivalent but slightly more precise regarding the 'management' aspect (which is limited to notification preferences rather than full report management). However, the original goal's phrasing 'Monitor and Manage' is acceptable in this context as 'Manage' refers to managing the notification settings and viewing the report history/status, which are the only management capabilities afforded to the citizen for their own reports. The goal is distinct from 'Communicate with Administration' (which covers active messaging) and 'Monitor Community Issues' (which covers other citizens' reports). It is not redundant with other goals and correctly captures the stakeholder intention of staying informed and controlling notification preferences for their specific submissions. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the 'Manage' aspect of the parent HLG (retrieving and updating notification preferences) but fail to cover the 'Monitor' aspect. The documentation explicitly states that citizens receive notifications on the platform at every state change and can view the status of their reports. The current LLG 'RetrieveReportProgressHistory' is a specific implementation detail (fetching a chronological list) that is not explicitly documented as a distinct feature (the doc mentions viewing status and receiving notifications, not necessarily a detailed history log of all actions/comments). More critically, there is no LLG for 'Viewing Report Status' or 'Receiving/Viewing Platform Notifications', which are the primary mechanisms for monitoring described in Section C. The parent goal requires citizens to 'stay informed about the progress and status', which entails a capability to view the current status and receive/view notifications, not just a historical log. Therefore, the essential capability of viewing the current status/notifications is missing.

It is not redundant with other goals and correctly captures the stakeholder intention of staying informed and controlling notification preferences for their specific submissions.

The current LLGs cover the 'Manage' aspect of the parent HLG (retrieving and updating notification preferences) but fail to cover the 'Monitor' aspect. The documentation explicitly states that citizens receive notifications on the platform at every state change and can view the status of their reports. The current LLG 'RetrieveReportProgressHistory' is a specific implementation detail (fetching a chronological list) that is not explicitly documented as a distinct feature (the doc mentions viewing status and receiving notifications, not necessarily a detailed history log of all actions/comments). More critically, there is no LLG for 'Viewing Report Status' or 'Receiving/Viewing Platform Notifications', which are the primary mechanisms for monitoring described in Section C. The parent goal requires citizens to 'stay informed about the progress and status', which entails a capability to view the current status and receive/view notifications, not just a historical log. Therefore, the essential capability of viewing the current status/notifications is missing.
low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback: Replace 'RetrieveReportProgressHistory' with a more general 'ViewReportStatusAndNotifications' or split it into 'ViewCurrentReportStatus' and 'ViewPlatformNotifications'. The documentation supports viewing the status (via the map/table or report page) and receiving/viewing notifications on the platform. The specific 'history log' is not explicitly documented as a feature for citizens, whereas status viewing and notification reception are core to the 'Monitor' requirement.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current HLG 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' semantically entails the outcome of the retired HLG 'Receive Report Updates'. The description explicitly states that citizens receive notifications on the platform and via email (configurable) for state changes, and can view the status of their reports. The current HLG covers 'staying informed about progress and status' and 'controlling how they receive these notifications', which fully encompasses the functionality of receiving updates. No other actor-level responsibilities from the project description are left uncovered by the current HLG list.

branch_001.rationale: The initial goals (registration, account activation, and profile setup) are foundational steps that establish a citizen's identity and presence within the system. These steps are necessary prerequisites for the subsequent, core functionality of submitting detailed reports about urban issues, which include textual descriptions, multimedia attachments, geographical location, and categorization. All these operations collectively serve the purpose of empowering citizens to effectively communicate and report problems in their urban environment.

branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the functionalities required for a citizen to engage in a two-way communication with a municipal operator concerning a specific report, including the ability to send messages, receive responses, and review the entire conversation history. This ensures transparency and effective resolution of reports through direct dialogue.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit anonymous reports
branch_003.rationale: Both low-level goals directly contribute to the overarching objective of providing and maintaining anonymity for citizens when they submit reports. One goal focuses on the user's ability to choose anonymity, and the other focuses on the system's responsibility to enforce it.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Access and Monitor Public Reports
branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe functionalities that allow citizens to discover (view, filter) and track (subscribe, unsubscribe) publicly available reports submitted by other citizens. These operations are all geared towards providing citizens with the means to stay informed about and engage with community-reported information.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Non-Registered Users to View and Filter Public Reports
branch_005.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe various ways a non-registered user can access, display, and refine their view of public reports. They cover different presentation formats (interactive map, summary table) and a filtering mechanism (geographical filter), all contributing to the overarching goal of allowing public access and exploration of these reports.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide Public Access to Reporting Statistics
branch_006.rationale: Both low-level goals describe functionalities for non-registered users to view different types of statistics related to reports. One focuses on categorical breakdowns, and the other on temporal trends, but both contribute to the overarching goal of making reporting data publicly accessible for informational purposes.

branch_007.rationale: These operations collectively describe the process by which office staff evaluate citizen reports and make a formal decision regarding their acceptance or rejection, including providing necessary justifications for rejections. They all contribute to the initial handling and disposition of incoming reports.

branch_008.rationale: All low-level goals describe actions related to setting or changing the status of a report at various stages of its lifecycle, from submission to completion or rejection. This ensures proper tracking and workflow management for reports.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Technical Office Staff to Monitor and Report on Report Progress
branch_009.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide technical office staff with comprehensive capabilities to view current status, track historical changes, and generate summary reports related to the progress of reports or issues. These operations are all essential for effective oversight, management, and communication regarding the lifecycle and resolution of reports within their office.

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions required by technical office staff to track the progress of a report from the initiation of active work to its successful completion, including documenting the specific details of how it was resolved. These operations are integral to overseeing and completing the resolution of a report.

branch_011.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage communication with external maintenance personnel regarding assigned reports
branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel concerning a specific report: sending messages, receiving responses, and reviewing the entire interaction history. These operations are all integral to effectively managing and tracking communication related to assigned reports.

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Assigned Reports for External Maintenance Personnel
branch_012.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps an external maintenance personnel takes to identify, understand, and formally accept responsibility for reports assigned to them. These operations are all part of the initial phase of managing an assigned report, from discovery to formal acknowledgment.

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate External Maintenance Personnel Reporting of Work Progress and Completion
branch_013.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions for external maintenance personnel to report the lifecycle of their assigned tasks. They cover initiating work, marking it as finished, and providing necessary evidence, all contributing to a comprehensive reporting process for maintenance activities.

branch_014.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Communicate with the Municipal Technical Office regarding Reports
branch_014.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential functionalities for external maintenance personnel to engage in two-way communication (sending and receiving messages) and maintain an auditable record (viewing history) with the municipal technical office concerning specific reports. They all contribute to establishing and managing this communication channel.

branch_015.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various administrative and configuration tasks performed by a municipal administrator. These tasks include managing data categories, defining operational rules, controlling user access, setting system-wide behaviors like notifications, and configuring external integrations. All these operations are essential for setting up, customizing, and maintaining the overall functionality and operational parameters of the system.

branch_016.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Municipal Administrator to Monitor and Analyze System Performance and Usage
branch_016.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various methods for the municipal administrator to access, customize, visualize, and export statistical data and reports. These operations are all geared towards providing the administrator with the necessary tools to monitor system performance, understand user interactions, evaluate system health, and conduct in-depth analysis of operational data.

branch_017.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate Citizen Report Evaluation and Disposition
branch_017.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process for the Organization Office Staff to access, thoroughly review, investigate, and ultimately decide on the validity and status (approve or reject) of citizen reports, ensuring proper handling and disposition within the system.

branch_018.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Information Flow for Submitted Reports
branch_018.rationale: These goals collectively aim to empower citizens to stay informed about the progress of their submitted reports and to control how they receive updates. llg_001 provides the detailed progress history, while llg_002 and llg_003 allow for viewing and customizing the notification delivery preferences, ensuring citizens have full control over their report-related information.

branch_019.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Resolution Process of Approved Citizen Reports
branch_019.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential activities for the Technical Office Staff to oversee and control the lifecycle of an approved citizen report. This includes assigning it for resolution, tracking its historical progress, and updating its current status, all of which are integral to managing its resolution effectively.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Communicate with Administration' is supported by the project description (Section C), which explicitly states that municipal operators can send messages to citizens and citizens can reply. However, the current hierarchy contains a sibling HLG 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' which is described as allowing citizens to 'stay informed about the progress and status... receive timely updates'. In the context of this system, 'updates' and 'communication' regarding a specific report are tightly coupled. The description in Section C groups notifications (state changes) and direct messaging (operator to citizen, citizen to operator) under the umbrella of strengthening trust and keeping citizens informed. The 'Monitor and Manage' HLG is broad enough to encompass the entire interaction loop regarding the citizen's own reports, including the ability to reply to messages. Keeping 'Communicate with Administration' as a separate HLG creates fragmentation, as it is a specific channel/mechanism within the broader outcome of managing and monitoring one's reports. The 'Monitor and Manage' HLG is the appropriate umbrella for all citizen-side interactions regarding their specific reports (viewing status, receiving notifications, and exchanging messages). Therefore, the specific communication goal is entailed by the broader monitoring/management goal.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

branch_016.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that the private section is accessible only to administrators and allows viewing charts and tables in addition to public statistics. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Municipal Administrator to Monitor and Analyze System Performance and Usage' captures the same intention but with slightly more precise terminology regarding the purpose (monitoring/analysis) rather than just access. However, the original goal is not materially defective; it correctly identifies the actor's need to view detailed statistical data for oversight. There is no broader sibling goal for the Municipal Administrator that encompasses this specific statistical oversight function (the other goal is 'Configure System Settings'). Therefore, the original goal is valid, supported, and independently scoped. The difference between 'Access' and 'Monitor/Analyze' is minor and does not warrant a rewrite, as accessing the data is the primary capability described, and the analysis is the implicit purpose. Keeping the original goal maintains consistency with the documented capability of viewing private statistics. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are not supported by the project description. Specifically, 'GenerateCustomStatisticalReports' (llg_002) implies a feature for defining parameters to generate tailored reports, which is not mentioned in the documentation; the system only describes viewing existing public and private statistics (charts and tables). 'ExportStatisticsData' (llg_003) is also unsupported, as there is no mention of exporting data in any format. 'ViewPerformanceDashboards' (llg_004) mentions 'system health metrics' and 'key performance indicators', which goes beyond the documented scope of 'number of reports per category' and 'trends over day, week, or month'. The only partially supported LLG is 'RetrieveAllReportStatistics' (llg_001), which aligns with viewing the comprehensive statistics available to administrators. Since three out of four LLGs introduce undocumented functionality, the decomposition is materially defective.

Based on the current sibling list, 'Assign Approved Report to Team' is the most distinct capability, but even that might overlap with workflow management. If 'Manage Approved Report Resolution' is to remain, its LLGs should not duplicate 'Track' or 'Update'.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements for the Technical Office Staff. The retired goal 'Assign Approved Reports' is fully entailed by the current goal 'Manage Approved Report Resolution', which explicitly includes 'initial assignment to the relevant internal or external teams'. The other retired goals ('Review Citizen Reports' and 'Receive Report Updates') belong to different actors (Organization Office Staff and Citizen, respectively) and are covered by their respective current HLGs ('Process Citizen Reports' and 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports'). No other actor-level responsibilities from the project description are left uncovered.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues
branch_001.rationale: The initial goals (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003) focus on establishing and personalizing a citizen's account, which is a prerequisite for participating in the system. The subsequent goals (llg_004, llg_005, llg_006, llg_007) detail the process of submitting comprehensive reports about urban issues. Together, these operations form a complete flow for citizens to engage with a platform designed for reporting community problems.

branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the functionalities required for a citizen to engage in a two-way communication with a municipal operator concerning a specific report, including the ability to send messages, receive responses, and review the entire conversation history. This ensures transparency and effective resolution of reports through direct dialogue.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit anonymous reports
branch_003.rationale: Both low-level goals directly contribute to the overarching objective of providing and maintaining anonymity for citizens when they submit reports. One goal focuses on the user's ability to choose anonymity, and the other focuses on the system's responsibility to enforce it.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Access and Monitor Public Reports
branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe functionalities that allow citizens to discover (view, filter) and track (subscribe, unsubscribe) publicly available reports submitted by other citizens. These operations are all geared towards providing citizens with the means to stay informed about and engage with community-reported information.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Non-Registered Users to View and Filter Public Reports
branch_005.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe various ways a non-registered user can access, display, and refine their view of public reports. They cover different presentation formats (interactive map, summary table) and a filtering mechanism (geographical filter), all contributing to the overarching goal of allowing public access and exploration of these reports.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable non-registered users to view various report statistics
branch_006.rationale: Both low-level goals describe functionalities for non-registered users to access and view different types of statistics related to reports: one by category and another showing trends over time. They collectively contribute to the broader goal of providing comprehensive statistical insights to non-registered users.

branch_007.rationale: These operations collectively describe the process by which office staff evaluate citizen reports and make a formal decision regarding their acceptance or rejection, including providing necessary justifications for rejections. They all contribute to the initial handling and disposition of incoming reports.

branch_008.rationale: These low-level goals collectively define the various states a report can assume throughout its lifecycle, from initial submission to different stages of processing and eventual outcomes. They describe how the report's status is set and updated, either automatically by the system or manually by office staff, to reflect its current position in the workflow.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Technical Office Staff to Monitor and Report on Report Progress
branch_009.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide technical office staff with comprehensive capabilities to view current status, track historical changes, and generate summary reports related to the progress of reports or issues. These operations are all essential for effective oversight, management, and communication regarding the lifecycle and resolution of reports within their office.

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps for technical office staff to track the progress and document the outcome of work performed on a report, from the initiation of active work to its successful completion and the detailed recording of how it was resolved. They all contribute to effectively managing the lifecycle of a report's resolution.

branch_011.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage communication with external maintenance personnel regarding assigned reports
branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel concerning a specific report: sending messages, receiving responses, and reviewing the entire interaction history. These operations are all integral to effectively managing and tracking communication related to assigned reports.

branch_012.rationale: These operations collectively enable external maintenance personnel to discover, understand, and formally accept responsibility for intervention reports assigned to them, forming the initial phase of their task management workflow.

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Update Maintenance Report Progress and Completion
branch_013.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions for external maintenance personnel to accurately reflect the progress of their assigned work, from commencement to completion, and to provide necessary evidence for the resolution of a maintenance report.

branch_014.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage communication between external maintenance personnel and the municipal technical office regarding reports
branch_014.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the various facets of communication (sending, receiving, and reviewing history) that external maintenance personnel engage in with the municipal technical office, all specifically pertaining to reports. Therefore, the overarching goal is to manage this communication effectively.

branch_015.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Municipal Administrator to Monitor and Analyze System Performance and Usage
branch_015.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various methods for the municipal administrator to access, customize, visualize, and export statistical data and reports. These operations are all geared towards providing the administrator with the necessary tools to monitor system performance, understand user interactions, evaluate system health, and conduct in-depth analysis of operational data.

branch_016.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for Organization Office Staff to handle incoming citizen reports, from initial identification and detailed examination to making a final decision (approval or rejection) and updating the report's status. They cover accessing, reviewing, investigating, and ultimately resolving the status of citizen reports.

branch_017.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Monitor and Control Information Flow Regarding Their Submitted Reports
branch_017.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide citizens with the ability to both observe the progress and details of their submitted reports (monitoring) and to customize how they receive updates and notifications about these reports (controlling information flow). llg_001 focuses on viewing the report's history, while llg_002 and llg_003 address the management of notification preferences.

branch_018.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Resolution Process of Approved Citizen Reports
branch_018.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential activities for the Technical Office Staff to oversee and control the lifecycle of an approved citizen report. This includes assigning it for resolution, tracking its historical progress, and updating its current status, all of which are integral to managing its resolution effectively.

branch_019.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage System Configuration and User Access Control
branch_019.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the Municipal Administrator's responsibilities for setting up and maintaining the system's operational rules and parameters (llg_001 to llg_004), as well as managing user accounts (llg_005 to llg_010) and controlling their access and permissions through roles (llg_011 to llg_014). These operations are all fundamental aspects of system administration, ensuring the system operates correctly and securely, and that users have appropriate access.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' is supported by the project description, which details the process of selecting a location, filling out a form, and attaching photos. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues' suggests a broader scope that includes registration. While registration is a prerequisite, the specific functional outcome of 'submitting reports' is distinct from 'registering'. More importantly, looking at the sibling goals, 'Maintain Report Anonymity' is a specific option *during* the submission process. The current HLG 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' is a valid, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome. It is not redundant with 'Monitor Community Issues' (viewing others) or 'Communicate with Administration' (post-submission interaction). The goal is appropriately scoped as a primary citizen action. The reconstruction's inclusion of registration is arguably a separate administrative prerequisite rather than part of the 'reporting' intention itself, though they are closely linked. Given the rubric, the original goal is precise and supported. It represents the core value proposition for the citizen. It is not fragmented because 'Maintain Report Anonymity' is a specific constraint/feature of the submission, not a separate workflow phase that warrants its own HLG if it were just a checkbox, but here it is listed as a separate HLG. Wait, if 'Maintain Report Anonymity' is a separate HLG, does 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' cover the non-anonymous part? Or is 'Submit' the umbrella? The description says 'The system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous'. This is part of the submission flow. Having 'Maintain Report Anonymity' as a separate HLG might be over-fragmentation. However, the question is about 'Submit Urban Issue Reports'. Is it too narrow? It covers the act of reporting. The sibling 'Maintain Report Anonymity' is a specific aspect. If we keep 'Submit', it should ideally encompass the anonymity choice. But since 'Maintain Report Anonymity' exists as a sibling, 'Submit' might be seen as the general action. The reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues' is broader. Is registration part of the 'Report' goal? Usually, registration is a separate goal 'Register for the System'. The current list does NOT have a 'Register' HLG for the Citizen. The Citizen's HLGs are: Submit, Monitor Own, Communicate, Maintain Anonymity, Monitor Community. Registration is missing as a distinct HLG. The reconstruction tries to merge it. However, 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' is a very standard, clear HLG. The lack of a 'Register' HLG is a gap in the *other* goals, not necessarily a defect in *this* goal. This goal is supported and distinct. It is not a workflow fragment of a larger 'Manage Citizen Account' goal because no such umbrella exists. It is a primary functional goal. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain a material defect. LLG llg_003 ('UploadCitizenProfilePhoto') is unsupported by the documentation for this specific goal. The project description states that citizens can upload a personal photo in the 'user settings panel' (Section C), which is a profile management capability distinct from the act of submitting a report. It is not a prerequisite for or part of the 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' workflow. Additionally, the parent goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' explicitly entails the capability to choose whether the report is anonymous, as described in Section A ('the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous'). This essential capability is absent from the current LLGs and is not covered by the sibling HLG 'Maintain Report Anonymity' in a way that allows it to be excluded from the submission flow's decomposition, as the anonymity choice is made *during* the submission process. Therefore, the decomposition is incomplete and contains an unsupported element.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Communicate with Administration' is supported by the documentation (Section C: 'municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply'). However, it is materially over-fragmented. The sibling goal 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' explicitly includes the intention to 'stay informed about the progress and status of their submitted reports, receive timely updates... fostering transparency and trust'. The communication channel (messaging) is a primary mechanism for these updates and interactions. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, the ability to exchange messages regarding a specific report is a functional capability that serves the broader stakeholder outcome of monitoring and managing the report lifecycle. Keeping 'Communicate with Administration' as a separate HLG creates redundancy with 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' and 'Monitor Community Issues' (which also involves following reports). The messaging feature is not an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome distinct from the management/monitoring of the report; it is the *means* by which the administration interacts with the citizen about the report. Therefore, it should be removed to consolidate the hierarchy under the broader management/monitoring goals.

Keeping it separate creates redundancy and fragments the 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' workflow. Therefore, it should be removed to consolidate the hierarchy under the broader submission goal.

The original High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration' is well-supported by the project description, which explicitly assigns the Municipal Administrator responsibilities for system configuration (e.g., automatic assignment rules) and user management. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage System Configuration and User Access Control' is semantically equivalent and accurately reflects the documented capabilities (LLGs for configuring rules and managing user accounts/roles). The goal represents a distinct, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome (system administration) that is separate from the other Municipal Administrator goal ('Access Comprehensive Statistics'). It is not redundant with other actors' goals, nor is it a fragmented workflow step. The original goal is precise, supported, and appropriately scoped.

low_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration'. The documentation explicitly supports the configuration of automatic report assignment rules (Section B, Case 1 Note), which is covered by llg_001 to llg_003. The documentation explicitly assigns the Municipal Administrator responsibility for user management and access control (Actor Description), which is covered by the user account management LLGs (llg_005 to llg_010) and role management LLGs (llg_011 to llg_014). llg_004 ('Update System Behavior Parameter') is a reasonable abstraction for general system configuration implied by the actor's responsibility for 'system configuration'. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are unsupported or contradictory to the documentation.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements and actor responsibilities documented in the project description. The retired goal 'Configure System Settings' is fully entailed by the current goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration', which explicitly includes configuring system behaviors like automatic report assignment rules. The retired goal 'Receive Report Updates' is covered by 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports'. The retired goal 'Assign Approved Reports' is covered by 'Manage Approved Report Resolution'. The retired goal 'Review Citizen Reports' is covered by 'Process Citizen Reports'. All other actor capabilities (Citizen, Non-Registered User, Organization Office Staff, Technical Office Staff, External Maintenance Personnel, Municipal Administrator) are accurately represented by the current HLG list without significant omissions or unsupported additions.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues
branch_001.rationale: The initial goals (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003) focus on establishing and personalizing a citizen's account, which is a prerequisite for participating in the system. The subsequent goals (llg_004, llg_005, llg_006, llg_007) detail the process of submitting comprehensive reports about urban issues. Together, these operations form a complete flow for citizens to engage with a platform designed for reporting community problems.

branch_002.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the process by which office staff assesses incoming citizen reports to determine their validity and appropriateness. This includes the actions of formally accepting a report, formally declining a report, and providing a mandatory explanation when a report is rejected, all of which are integral steps in the initial validation and screening of citizen submissions.

branch_003.rationale: These low-level goals collectively define the various states a report can assume throughout its lifecycle, from initial submission to different stages of processing and eventual outcomes. They describe how the report's status is set and updated, either automatically by the system or manually by office staff, to reflect its current position in the workflow.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Technical Office Staff to Monitor and Report on Report Progress
branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide technical office staff with comprehensive capabilities to view current status, track historical changes, and generate summary reports related to the progress of reports or issues. These operations are all essential for effective oversight, management, and communication regarding the lifecycle and resolution of reports within their office.

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions required by technical office staff to track the progress of a report from the initiation of active work to its successful completion, including documenting the specific details of how it was resolved. These operations are integral to overseeing and completing the resolution of a report.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage communication with external maintenance personnel regarding assigned reports
branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel concerning a specific report: sending messages, receiving responses, and reviewing the entire interaction history. These operations are all integral to effectively managing and tracking communication related to assigned reports.

branch_007.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Assigned Reports for External Maintenance Personnel
branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps an external maintenance personnel takes to identify, understand, and formally accept responsibility for reports assigned to them. These operations are all part of the initial phase of managing an assigned report, from discovery to formal acknowledgment.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Update Maintenance Report Progress and Completion
branch_008.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions for external maintenance personnel to accurately reflect the progress of their assigned work, from commencement to completion, and to provide necessary evidence for the resolution of a maintenance report.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Communicate with the Municipal Technical Office regarding Reports
branch_009.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential functionalities for external maintenance personnel to engage in two-way communication (sending and receiving messages) and maintain an auditable record (viewing history) with the municipal technical office concerning specific reports. They all contribute to establishing and managing this communication channel.

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various methods for a municipal administrator to interact with and process system data, including retrieving comprehensive statistics, generating tailored reports, exporting data for external analysis, and viewing interactive dashboards. All these actions contribute to the overarching objective of understanding and evaluating the system's performance, usage, and health through data analysis.

branch_011.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for Organization Office Staff to handle incoming citizen reports, from initial identification and detailed examination to making a final decision (approval or rejection) and updating the report's status. They cover accessing, reviewing, investigating, and ultimately resolving the status of citizen reports.

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Information Flow for Submitted Reports
branch_012.rationale: These goals collectively aim to empower citizens to stay informed about the progress of their submitted reports and to control how they receive updates. llg_001 provides the detailed progress history, while llg_002 and llg_003 allow for viewing and customizing the notification delivery preferences, ensuring citizens have full control over their report-related information.

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Resolution Process of Approved Citizen Reports
branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions for the Technical Office Staff to oversee and progress approved citizen reports. This includes assigning them to teams, tracking their historical progress and current status, and updating their status as they move towards resolution and closure.

branch_014.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage System Configuration and User Access
branch_014.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the administrative responsibilities of the Municipal Administrator. These responsibilities fall into two main categories: configuring system behavior (such as defining report assignment rules and modifying system parameters) and managing user accounts and their associated roles and permissions. Together, these operations ensure the system operates correctly and securely, controlling both its functionality and who can access and perform actions within it.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REWRITE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' is supported by the documentation but is materially over-fragmented. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to Register and Report Urban Issues' correctly identifies that registration is a prerequisite for submitting reports and that these capabilities jointly realize the citizen's primary intention to engage with the platform. The current hierarchy lacks a single umbrella goal for the citizen's initial engagement (registration + submission), splitting them into distinct phases. According to the consolidation audit, when a hierarchy is fragmented and no sibling is a valid umbrella, the broadest suitable goal should be rewritten to cover the end-to-end intention. Therefore, the original goal should be rewritten to encompass both registration and report submission.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

branch_012.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is well-supported by the project description, specifically Section C (Citizen Updates), which details how citizens receive notifications, view status changes, and manage notification preferences (email toggles). The goal correctly captures the stakeholder intention of maintaining transparency and trust through information flow management. While the bottom-up reconstruction suggests a slight refinement to 'Manage Information Flow', the original goal's phrasing 'Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is a standard and acceptable abstraction for the capabilities of viewing status, receiving updates, and configuring notification settings. It is distinct from 'Submit Urban Issue Reports' (creation) and does not overlap with other Citizen goals. The goal is independently scoped and represents a valid end-to-end outcome for the citizen regarding post-submission engagement. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the core capabilities of monitoring report progress (llg_001) and managing notification preferences (llg_002, llg_003). However, the parent HLG 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' and the project description (Section C) explicitly state that citizens can 'receive updates... through various channels' and that 'municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply.' The current LLGs do not include the capability to view these messages or to reply to them. While llg_001 mentions 'comments', it is framed as a 'progress history' which typically implies a read-only log of system events and status changes, not an interactive messaging thread. The ability to actively engage in a dialogue (viewing and replying to operator messages) is a distinct and essential part of 'managing' the report interaction as described. Therefore, the capability to view and reply to messages is missing.

branch_013.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Approved Report Resolution' is a valid umbrella goal for the Technical Office Staff. It correctly encompasses the end-to-end process of handling reports after they have been approved by the Organization Office. The sibling goals 'Track Report Progress', 'Update Report Status', and 'Facilitate Internal Communication' are specific workflow phases or capabilities that are fully contained within the broader intention of managing the resolution process. According to the consolidation audit, these fragmented goals should be subsumed under the broader umbrella. The original goal is supported by the description (Section B and C) and represents the primary stakeholder outcome for this actor. Therefore, it should be kept as the umbrella goal, and the more specific sibling goals would ideally be removed or treated as sub-goals in a refined hierarchy, but for the purpose of evaluating this specific artifact, the original goal is correct and well-scoped. The current LLGs cover the core operational capabilities of the Technical Office Staff: assigning reports (llg_001), tracking progress/history (llg_002), and updating status (llg_003). However, the parent HLG description explicitly includes 'facilitating necessary internal communication' as a key component of managing the resolution process. Section B of the description states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. To be fully supported by the parent's stated scope, the LLGs must include the ability to exchange comments/information with external maintenance personnel. Therefore, a material omission exists.

branch_014.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration' is well-supported by the project description. The description explicitly states that the Municipal Administrator is responsible for system configuration (e.g., configuring automatic report assignment rules) and user management. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage System Configuration and User Access' captures the same core intention but is slightly less comprehensive in its naming compared to the original, which explicitly mentions 'Administration' covering both configuration and user management. The original goal is appropriately scoped as an independent administrative function distinct from the operational goals of other actors (like processing reports or tracking progress). It is not a fragment of a larger workflow but a distinct administrative responsibility. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) provide a comprehensive and well-supported decomposition of the High-Level Goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration'. The LLGs correctly cover the two main pillars of this HLG as described in the project documentation: 1) System Configuration, specifically the management of automatic report assignment rules (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003) which is explicitly mentioned in Section B ('Automatic assignment... is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator'), and general system behavior parameters (llg_004). 2) User Management, covering the full lifecycle of user accounts (create, update, deactivate, activate, retrieve) and role management (assign, revoke, retrieve roles). These capabilities are explicitly entailed by the actor description ('responsible for system configuration, user management') and the system's need to control access for various roles (Citizens, Office Staff, Technical Staff, External Personnel). There are no unsupported LLGs; all are standard administrative functions necessary for the described system. missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS_FOUND. The audit reveals that the removal of specific High-Level Goals (HLGs) for the 'Non-Registered User' and 'Citizen' actors has left documented functional requirements uncovered by the current HLG list. 

1. **Non-Registered User Gaps**: The project description explicitly states that 'Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table' and that 'Public statistics are... visible to non-registered users.' The current HLG list contains no goals for the 'Non-Registered User' actor. The previously removed goals 'Access Public Report Information' and 'View Public System Statistics' covered these distinct, externally visible capabilities. While 'Citizen' can also view these, the 'Non-Registered User' is a distinct actor with a specific responsibility to access public data without authentication, which is not entailed by any current HLG.

2. **Citizen Gaps**: The project description states that 'Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications'. The previously removed goal 'Monitor Community Issues' covered this specific capability of following *other* citizens' reports. The current HLG 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is scoped to 'their submitted reports' (their own). Following other citizens' reports is a distinct stakeholder outcome (community engagement/transparency) that is not semantically entailed by managing one's own reports. Additionally, the capability to 'Communicate with Administration' (reply to messages from operators) was removed. While 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' mentions receiving updates, the explicit two-way communication channel (municipal operators sending messages to citizens, and citizens replying) is a distinct interaction responsibility that was covered by the removed 'Communicate with Administration' goal and is not fully entailed by the current monitoring goal, which focuses on status updates and notification preferences.

missing_goal_requests.generation_project_description: Generate an HLG for accessing public report information, specifically viewing the interactive map and summary table of approved reports without registration, as explicitly required for non-registered users in Section C.
Generate an HLG for viewing public system statistics, including report counts per category and trends, which are explicitly stated to be visible to non-registered users in Section D.
Generate an HLG for monitoring community issues, specifically allowing logged-in citizens to follow other citizens' open reports and receive notifications about them, as described in Section C.

Generate an HLG for communicating with administration, enabling citizens to receive messages from municipal operators regarding their reports and reply to them through the platform, as described in Section C.

These operations are all fundamental aspects of system administration, ensuring the system operates correctly and securely, and that users have appropriate access.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Approve or Reject Reports' is semantically redundant with the existing sibling goal 'Process Citizen Reports' for the same actor (Organization Office Staff). Both goals describe the same end-to-end stakeholder intention: the initial review and disposition of citizen reports (acceptance or rejection with justification). 'Process Citizen Reports' is a broader and more accurate umbrella term that encompasses the review, decision, and justification steps. Keeping both creates unnecessary fragmentation of a single workflow phase. According to the consolidation audit, if a broader sibling already entails the original goal, the original should be removed to maintain a clean, non-redundant hierarchy.

branch_009.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that the Municipal Administrator can access private statistics including charts and tables in addition to public ones. However, the goal is fragmented. The sibling goal 'Manage System Configuration and Administration' covers the administrative duties (configuration, user management), while 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' covers the analytical/monitoring duties. These are distinct stakeholder outcomes: one is about maintaining the system's operational parameters, and the other is about gaining insight into system performance and usage. They are not sub-tasks of each other; an administrator can configure the system without viewing statistics, and view statistics without changing configuration. Therefore, 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' is an independently scoped, valid High-Level Goal. The reconstruction 'Analyze System Operational Data' is slightly more generic but semantically equivalent. The original goal is precise and well-scoped. It should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Access Comprehensive Statistics' is explicitly supported by Section D of the project description, which states that the private section allows administrators to view 'charts and tables' in addition to public statistics. However, the current LLGs introduce capabilities that are not documented: 'GenerateCustomStatisticalReports' (llg_002) implies a report generation engine not mentioned in the text; 'ExportStatisticsData' (llg_003) implies data export functionality which is not stated; and 'ViewPerformanceDashboards' (llg_004) uses terminology ('dashboards', 'KPIs', 'system health') that goes beyond the documented 'charts and tables' for report statistics. The documentation only supports viewing the specific statistical data (reports per category, trends) in chart and table formats. Therefore, the LLGs contain unsupported additions and should be regenerated to strictly reflect the documented capability of viewing private statistics (charts and tables).

branch_011.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Enable Citizens to Monitor and Manage Their Submitted Reports' is well-supported by the documentation. Section C explicitly details how citizens receive updates on their own reports (notifications, emails, messages) and can view their status on the map/table. The goal captures the stakeholder intention of staying informed and controlling notification preferences. It is distinct from 'Register and Report' (creation phase) and does not overlap with other Citizen HLGs in a way that causes redundancy. The reconstruction is semantically equivalent but slightly less precise regarding the 'management' aspect (which includes viewing status and controlling notifications). The original is clear, supported, and appropriately scoped. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs are insufficient and partially unsupported. 1) 'RetrieveReportProgressHistory' (llg_001) is unsupported: The documentation states citizens receive notifications at state changes and can view reports on a map/table, but it does not explicitly describe a feature for citizens to fetch a 'chronological list of all status changes, actions, and comments' for their own reports. While they can see the current status, a detailed history log is not explicitly entailed. 2) 'RetrieveNotificationPreferences' (llg_002) is a minor CRUD operation that is arguably part of the management interface but is not an essential capability distinct from updating them; however, the main issue is omission. 3) Essential capabilities are missing: The parent goal is to 'Monitor' reports. Section C explicitly states that 'Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications'. This 'Follow Report' capability is a distinct, documented monitoring action that is absent from the current LLGs. Additionally, the ability to 'View Report Status' (current state) on the map/table is the primary monitoring mechanism described, which is not explicitly captured as an LLG (llg_001 implies a history log which is less supported than the current status view). The current set fails to capture the explicit 'Follow' capability and relies on an unsupported 'History' capability.
